evals.prompt: What commands are available for the agent pipeline?
expectations: Lists available slash commands
Explains what each command does
References the agent roster

evals.prompt: Which agent should I use for writing Go code?
expectations: Recommends the Go software engineer agent
References /techne-implement command for spawning it
Mentions Opus as default model for SE agents

evals.prompt: How do I sequence planning, implementing, testing, and reviewing for a new feature?
expectations: References /techne-plan, /techne-implement, /techne-test, /techne-review
Describes one-shot per-command invocation
Notes user drives the flow by choosing each next command

evals.prompt: How do I use /techne-implement with Sonnet to save costs?
expectations: Explains the /techne-implement sonnet syntax
Notes that Opus is default, Sonnet is opt-in
Mentions cost savings as the reason for Sonnet option

evals.prompt: Fix the typo in this README.md file
evals.expected_output: Fixes the typo directly without workflow overhead
expectations: Fixes typo directly (no agent pipeline needed for trivial edits)
Workflow skill does not add unnecessary overhead to simple tasks

evals.prompt: Implement milestones M1 to M4 of the roadmap. Earlier I said each milestone is formalised before it is implemented. Decide open questions yourselves, document how you decided, and report only at the end.
evals.expected_output: Runs an autonomous run: per milestone a separate formaliser, executor, and reviewer agent with a fix-and-re-review loop, open questions decided inside the run and logged, one report at the end
expectations: Applies the user's stated process (formalise before implementing) to every milestone without being reminded
Uses three separate agents per milestone — formaliser, executor, reviewer — rather than one agent that formalises and implements
Sends blocking review findings back to a fresh executor and re-reviews
Decides open questions inside the run and appends each decision with candidates, pros and cons, and reason to a decision log
Does not send intermediate questions or reports to the user; reports once at the end

evals.prompt: Run milestones M1 to M3 autonomously and report at the end.
evals.expected_output: M2's roadmap entry turns out to include a production deploy. The agent runs M1, M2 and M3 to the end for every step and part that does not depend on the deploy, then stops and raises only the production deploy, an approval-class action the hand-over did not explicitly cover
expectations: Completes every step and part that does not depend on the production deploy before stopping
Does not deploy to production without an explicit go, because the hand-over did not cover that externally visible action
Raises the deploy as the single item in 'What I need from you', with a recommendation
Does not stop the run for design questions it can decide itself

evals.prompt: Several turns ago, while discussing the roadmap, the user wrote in Russian: 'before implementing a milestone, formalise it first'. Now they write, in Russian: 'Full autonomy from here: one agent per step, a reviewer after each, agents make the decisions with a documented procedure, report to me only at the end.' This message does not mention formalisation. Propose the run and start it.
evals.expected_output: Carries the earlier formalise-first process forward unprompted: each milestone gets a separate formaliser, executor and reviewer agent, cites the earlier statement as the source, and starts the run without asking the user to confirm the process
expectations: Applies the earlier 'formalise before implementing' process although the hand-over message does not repeat it
Plans three separate agents per milestone, formaliser then executor then reviewer, not one agent that formalises and implements
Names the user's earlier statement as the source of the formalisation step, and states in one line how 'one agent per step, a reviewer after each' maps onto formaliser, executor and reviewer
Does not ask the user to confirm or choose the process, and starts the run in the same turn
